page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.6xlarge is a high-frequency compute instance driven by a 3.1 GHz Intel Xeon 8269CY processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. Deployed on a KVM hypervisor with dedicated CPU allocation, it provides 12 physical cores running up to 24 virtual CPUs via hyperthreading. The server is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 4.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Local disk storage is not included, requiring external network-attached storage configurations, while baseline network throughput is rated at 8 Gbps. Hardware capabilities include AVX-512 with VNNI vector extensions alongside AES cryptography support.

Across synthetic and application benchmarks, the ecs.hfg6.6xlarge performs within the middle 50% band relative to tested cloud instances. Multi-core testing yields a stress-ng score of 23015.19 and a PassMark CPU score of 23637.6, with single-core execution reaching 1438.39 in stress-ng and 1287.0 in Geekbench. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth measures 109.43 GB/sec and write bandwidth reaches 48.03 GB/sec. Application workload testing records 22.14 million Redis SET operations per second and 17.13 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation paired with high clock speeds offers balanced compute density for general-purpose execution. Omitting local NVMe storage relies on external network disks for persistence, which introduces storage latency considerations. This hardware configuration suits web serving, software compilation tasks, in-memory caching systems such as Redis, and general enterprise application hosting.
